member.name: T:Kmila.Shared.Models.FPGAClocking
member.summary: Represents the clocking resource specifications of an FPGA device. Clocking resources are essential for generating and distributing clock signals throughout the FPGA fabric.
member.remarks: Different FPGA families have varying clocking architectures: - Xilinx uses DCMs (Digital Clock Managers) and MMCMs (Mixed-Mode Clock Managers) - Altera/Intel uses PLLs (Phase-Locked Loops) - Lattice uses PLLs and dedicated clock networks

member.summary: Gets or sets the number of PLL (Phase-Locked Loop) units available.
member.remarks: PLLs are used to generate multiple clock frequencies from a single reference clock, perform clock multiplication/division, and phase shifting.

member.name: P:Kmila.Shared.Models.FPGAClocking.DcmMmcmCount
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of DCM/MMCM (Digital Clock Manager / Mixed-Mode Clock Manager) units available.
member.remarks: DCMs and MMCMs provide advanced clock management features including frequency synthesis, phase shifting, and duty cycle correction. Primarily found in Xilinx FPGAs.

member.name: P:Kmila.Shared.Models.FPGAClocking.MaxPllOutputMhz
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum PLL output frequency in MHz.
member.remarks: This represents the highest frequency that can be generated by the FPGA's clock management resources. Actual achievable frequencies depend on the specific design and timing constraints.

member.name: P:Kmila.Shared.Models.FPGAClocking.SystemClockMhz
member.summary: Optional override for the default simulation system clock in MHz. When present, Kmila uses this directly as the simulator's tick rate. When absent, the app derives a sensible default from (see ). Kept optional so existing bundled JSON files don't need migration — curriculum authors can opt-in per device.

member.name: M:Kmila.Shared.Models.FPGAClocking.GetDefaultSimClockMhz
member.summary: Effective default system-clock frequency (MHz) used by the simulator when the student hasn't set a per-project override.
member.remarks: Priority: explicit > heuristic > fallback 50 MHz. The PLL-based heuristic caps the clock at 100 MHz so a device advertising 1300 MHz PLL output doesn't push the simulator into millions-of-ticks territory for a 1 µs run.

member.summary:
GitHub Device Flow OAuth client + token store. Why Device Flow: it works without a server-side secret (we ship a public Client ID to the browser), and the user never has to paste a personal access token. The trade-off is the two-step UX — show a code, ask the user to type it on github.com — which we surface in .
Login is OPTIONAL. The app is fully usable signed-out; the only features that depend on auth are the in-app issue submission flow () and the "auto-send error reports" toggle. Tier 1 (copy diagnostics) and Tier 2 (open prefilled issue URL) in remain available either way.
Token storage uses 's settings table — same pattern as language / theme / tick-resolution — so it survives across sessions on a per-install basis. The token is stored as-is (no encryption); for a learning tool with optional login this matches the threat model. Users can sign out from the Settings page at any time, which deletes the row.
